speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources whether the Ministry will consider building more smoking rooms in all buildings with public access so as to contain second-hand smoke.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources whether the Ministry will consider implementing restrictions against smokers who smoke whilst on the move, such as walking or cycling, as they leave behind residual second-hand smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Smoking has been a significant and long-standing public health issue in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government has taken a multi-pronged approach to tackle tobacco addiction, such as by curtailing access to cigarettes, sustaining public education and imposing taxes on tobacco products.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that smoking will continue in Singapore and throughout the world and smokers need time to wean themselves off their habit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We must, therefore, continue to remind those who smoke of the health effects and also to be considerate in their actions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Smokers have generally observed the smoking prohibition in public places, such as hospitals, clinics, sports complexes, office buildings and shopping malls.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Notwithstanding this, the Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act allows for the provision of indoor smoking rooms in certain types of publicly-accessible premises, such as in entertainment outlets, provided that the smoking room is independently ventilated and not required to be used by any person in the course of his work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The need for smoking rooms should be determined by the managers of these premises as they have a legal duty to uphold the smoking prohibition rule within their premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Premises managers may also set up designated smoking areas (DSAs) in the outdoor areas of their premises, provided these are not places where smoking is prohibited.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To the Member’s question on imposing restrictions on those who smoke on the move, the Government has already taken steps in that direction.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Since 2013, smoking on pedestrian overhead bridges and under covered walkways has been prohibited.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The issue of smoking is one that requires all sectors of society to play their part.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Families and communities must come together to encourage smokers to quit and keep them on a smoke-free path.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Premises managers must observe their legal obligation to help enforce the smoking prohibition within their premises in consideration of their non-smoking clients and staff.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Smokers should also be considerate when smoking in public places, and smoke only in permitted areas so as not to adversely affect the health of others.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the ground, many people are still walking or cycling and smoking, affecting those behind them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will the Ministry consider holding a campaign to educate our smokers to be more gracious in public by exercising care to keep second-hand smoke from blowing towards others?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More importantly, beyond campaigns and to encourage smokers to be considerate, we hope that we can also help smokers to completely quit smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And in this regard, the Health Promotion Board has educational campaigns to raise awareness about the harmful effects of smoking.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It also has a "I Quit" campaign that it administers to help smokers to quit in more easily adaptable steps by breaking them down to help them in their journey to quit.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Passers-by and pedestrians who currently walk past outdoor designated smoking areas will also breathe in second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If we could have some DSAs within the buildings, it could reduce the harmful effects of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the same time, it will protect the smokers from the elements.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While we are trying to do our best to reduce smoking, it takes time.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Meanwhile, we should provide an avenue where both parties could co-exist but without affecting each other negatively.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, most of the buildings with public access are already smoke-free areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have no intention to mandate smoking rooms in these places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Notwithstanding this, the premises owner can designate smoking areas as long as these are not areas where smoking is prohibited.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, beyond five metres from the entrance or exit of a building which is a smoking-prohibited area, they could designate a DSA.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is actually being done, for instance, in Orchard Road, where we have implemented DSAs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regards to having a smoking area within a building, the issue is that, if you have a smoking room in a building, it will reduce the level of exposure of environmental tobacco smoke (ETS), but not completely.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Which is that these premises must have a separate ventilation system where the smoking room is, and it must not be an area where staff is required to be in, in the course of their work and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If these can be complied with, then the premises owner can designate a smoking room.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A supplementary question: a common complaint from residents is of neighbours smoking in their balconies or out of the windows of their flats, leading to smoke wafting into the flats of residents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What would the Ministry recommend to residents who suffer from such second-hand smoke?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our advice would be for the affected resident to have a discussion with the neighbour to try and resolve this amicably.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If not, the resident may get assistance from a Community Mediation Centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the end of the day, we need to urge and get the smokers to be socially responsible and to be considerate when smoking so as not to cause disamenities to others.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Families and friends of the smokers as well as the public, in general, could help to reinforce the right social norms, through nudges and reminders, in order to be able to try and address such issues.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I take the Senior Minister of State's note that enforcement is not the panacea and it probably cannot solve all the problems.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But without enforcement, it will not be a proper deterrent for many of the smokers because, clearly, they are socially not that responsible.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For example, since there are not enough enforcers on the ground, if members of the public do have evidence of frequent smokers at the same location, can they submit that for the National Environment Agency (NEA) to take actions against those offenders?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even as enforcement alone is not the panacea, we will continue with our enforcement actions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also work with the Town Councils as well as grassroots organisations to educate smokers and encourage them to be more considerate.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, if a resident has information or sees acts of errant smokers smoking in prohibited areas, they could provide the information to NEA.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, why is the pilot project DSA set up in Orchard Road?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is an area where many people may be subjected to second-hand smoke.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is a key reason why we have done it there.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are studying and evaluating the results, as I have said.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will take these into consideration in deciding on future plans for DSAs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to study the results of the DSA pilot in Orchard Road to determine how effective it is in reducing smoking in other public areas, getting smokers to be considerate to smoke only in the DSAs, as well as the location, design of DSAs and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regards to DSAs in residential areas, as I have said, we are looking into the feasibility of expanding designated non-smoking areas, but we will look at the study and see how we can scale this up.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Speaker, there is still a lot of people who are still smoking in our public parks and park connectors, and a lot of people who smoke when they are walking to work or to the Mass Rapid Transit stations.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would just like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the Ministry would look into increasing the messaging on this concern.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think this is quite similar to the questions posed by the other Members, including Ms Joan Pereira, about having a campaign to educate smokers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, we have extended smoking prohibition to common corridors, covered linkways, pedestrian overhead bridges.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, it is illegal to smoke in these places.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If there are persons who are doing this, as I have said, we do carry out enforcement actions, particularly in hotspot areas.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But beyond that, Members can provide us with further information on such errant smokers.
